status: method diagnostics, not a separate mathematical certificate

rejected_float64_probe.result: Direct float64 evaluation of the inverse's last row in the bay produced spurious huge increments (about 5.20e57 at N=1000).
rejected_float64_probe.interpretation: Catastrophic cancellation. These values were rejected; the final bay results use high-precision arb solves and a separate precision comparison. Float64 evaluation at L alone did not reveal this error.

failed_checked_LU_probe.interpretation: Unsuccessful interval elimination at this precision; NOT a claim that the exact matrix is singular. Checked preconditioned solves on the same exact model subsequently succeeded.

successful_small_LU_probe.result: finite enclosures for both the last column and last row

certificate_methods.N200_N600: two checked default arb_mat.solve calls; saved data retained
certificate_methods.N800_N1000: one checked arb_mat.inv reused for the last row and last column
certificate_methods.whole_circle: complete finite Taylor polynomial, no quadrature or remainder truncation

intentional_checkpoints: The first large loop was stopped after saving N=600 to avoid computing its expensive preconditioner twice. The second loop was stopped after saving N=800 so that N=1000 could also certify the full vector G with the same checked inverse.
